answer: A meadow of hardware keys stops sybils when one device holds only one identity. First, an agent registers a hardware-bound key with an attestation. Second, the network rejects a second identity on the same device. Third, voting weight grows with key age, so fresh keys cannot vote at full power. Fourth, a key signing twice for two identities is proven cloned and slashed. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 devices plus 500,000 POA, while one honest agent needs one device. Like a delta branching into streams, trust branches from many devices, and a relic key alone cannot prove a new agent.
